background.task:
The scenario ran end-to-end against the real local backend (dev mode, server `http://127.0.0.1:8283`, health UP) with MockSite already serving on port 18080. A fresh headless session (`-s state-eval`) was opened on the interactive fixture and all ten steps were executed.

**Acceptance criteria outcome:**

| AC | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 `is visible` | ⚠️ Partially | `true` / `false` / no-match→`false` all correct, **but every `false` exits 0** — a false assertion is silently readable as success; no exit-code contract is documented in `--help`, `--help-json`, SKILL.md or README (contrast: `snapshot grep` documents exit 1 on zero matches). |
| AC2 `is enabled` | ⚠️ Partially | `true`/`false` correct, but a missing/invalid selector returns `null`, not `false` like its two siblings. |
| AC3 check/uncheck | ✅ | Round trip verified against both `is checked` and `window.__browser4State.checkbox`. |
| AC4 focus | ✅ | `document.activeElement.id` = `fill-target`. |
| AC5 scrollintoview | ✅ | scrollY 0→1335; box y 2159→824 (inside 1080px viewport). |
| AC6 highlight | ✅ | Inline `outline: rgb(255, 87, 34) solid 3px` on target only (sibling untouched). |
| AC7 pushstate | ✅ | pathname changed, `readyState: complete`, DOM intact (checkbox + outline survived), `page-info` shows new URL. |
| AC8 explicit failures | ❌ Partially | Missing arguments all fail correctly (exit 1 + usage). Bad selectors: `check`/`uncheck`/`click` print `✓` and exit 0 (silent pass), `focus` exits 0 silently; `scrollintoview`/`highlight`/`select` exit 1 naming the selector but with misleading labels/dumps. |

The functional core of this scenario works well, but the scripting contract (exit codes, silent no-ops) has real defects — the two answers the scenario explicitly asks for are both negative: exit codes are **not** documented anywhere a script author would look, and a false assertion **is** silently readable as success.

assessment.mostConfusingAspects: For a first-time user: (1) `is visible/enabled/checked` print true/false but always exit 0, with no exit-code contract anywhere a script author would look — and the sibling `is enabled` prints null where the others print false; (2) `check`/`uncheck`/`click` print '✓ Checked/Clicked' for selectors that match nothing, and `focus` does nothing with no message at all; (3) missing-element failures from highlight/scrollintoview surface as '[TIMEOUT] browser_evaluate failed' with a Java signature dump, which misattributes the cause and the command name; (4) `--help <cmd> --examples` claims the backend is down while it is demonstrably up; (5) `list` shows '-' for live sessions, the documented marker for a dead backend.
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Make silent failures loud: resolve the target for click/check/uncheck/focus and fail non-zero with the existing 'No element matches selector "<sel>"' message (BrowserTabToolExecutor already has the helper). 2) Add --fail-on-false (or document an exit-code contract) to the is-* assertions and document the output of each command. 3) Fix error classification/message hygiene so a missing element is not labeled TIMEOUT and never dumps internal Java signatures or tool names. 4) Return plain JSON {x,y,width,height} from `get box` and align the help text. 5) Never print a ✓ confirmation without verifying the action actually landed.

issues.title: check/uncheck/click/focus report success on selectors that match nothing

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval check "#no-such-element-abc" (repeat with uncheck/click/focus, and with a garbage selector `check "???"`) on http://localhost:18080/b4/mcp-tool-controller-interactive-fixture.html

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Non-zero exit and an error message naming the selector (AC8: 'no silent pass'); the ✓ confirmation must not print when no element was acted on.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: `check` printed '✓ Checked #no-such-element-abc' and exited 0; `uncheck`/`click` printed '✓ Unchecked/Clicked …' exit 0; `focus` exited 0 with no message at all. They are true no-ops: document.activeElement stayed 'fill-target' and window.__browser4State.checkbox kept its prior value. Even `check "???"` printed '✓ Checked ???' exit 0.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The tool executor dispatches straight to the driver (driver.check/uncheck/click/focus); the driver returns without error when the selector cannot be resolved (Browser4WebDriver.click resolves a hover point, gets null, and falls back to the upstream super.click which no-ops). The tool call therefore reports OK, and the CLI prints its unconditional success confirmation in main.rs (~8311-8351) without verifying the action landed. The executor already has the right helper — elementNotFoundMessage() at BrowserTabToolExecutor.kt:774, used by `select` — but click/check/uncheck/focus never call it.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-agentic/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agentic/tools/builtin/BrowserTabToolExecutor.kt ("click" ~1545, "focus" ~1304, "check" ~1854, "uncheck" ~1864); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:8311 (success-confirmation block)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Before dispatching click/check/uncheck/focus, resolve the target (driver.exists(selector)) and throw elementNotFoundMessage(selector) — the existing message already names the selector and gives ref-staleness guidance
- Alternatively make movePointerToClickTarget / focus fail loudly instead of returning null/silently
- Only print the '✓ Checked/Clicked …' line after the backend confirms the element was resolved (e.g. return the resolved ref from the tool)
- Add e2e coverage: every action command on a non-matching selector must exit non-zero

issues.title: Assertion commands exit 0 when the result is false/null — no scriptable failure signal, and no documentation

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval is visible "#hidden-target"; echo $?   (also `is visible "#no-such-element-xyz"`, `is enabled "#disabled-target"`, `is checked "#check-target"`)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A documented way for scripts to distinguish a false assertion from success (AC1: 'a false assertion must not be silently readable as success in a script').

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: All three commands print the value and exit 0 in every case. --json returns {"status":"ok","command":"is-visible","output":{"result":"false"}} — still exit 0. No opt-in flag exists (--fail-on-false is silently ignored, see the unknown-flag issue). The exit-code contract is documented nowhere: `--help`, `--help-json`, SKILL.md, README.md and quick-patterns.md all omit it. Contrast: `snapshot grep` documents 'Zero matches = exit 1', and the project's own audit scenarios build exit codes by hand via `| grep -q` pipelines.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The is-* commands are thin wrappers around MCP tool calls (CommandDef entries with no options, commands.rs ~2190-2231); the printed value is only text and process exit is driven solely by transport/tool-call errors, never by the boolean result. No assertion flag was added to the CommandDefs.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs (is-visible/is-enabled/is-checked CommandDefs); result handling in cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add an opt-in `--fail-on-false` (or `--assert`) flag that exits 1 when the assertion is false/null, keeping the default for backward compatibility
- Document the exit-code contract on each command's help page and in SKILL.md / README ('prints true/false; exits 0 unless --fail-on-false is given')
- At minimum, document the `--json` + output.result parsing route for scripts
- Fix `is enabled` to return false (see separate issue) so the flag has a uniform contract

issues.title: is enabled returns null instead of false for a missing or invalid selector

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval is enabled "#missing-xyz"   -> null ; ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval is enabled "["   -> null

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: false, consistent with `is visible` and `is checked` (both print false for the same selectors), and consistent with the 'no match = false' rule in AC1.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Prints null, exit 0. In --json it becomes the string "result":"null", so even machine consumers get a different type than the sibling commands.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The "isEnabled" branch has no dedicated driver method: it calls driver.evaluateValue(selector, "function() { return !(this.disabled || this.readOnly); }") (BrowserTabToolExecutor.kt:1295-1301), which returns null when the element cannot be resolved. isVisible/isChecked go through driver methods that return false.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-agentic/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agentic/tools/builtin/BrowserTabToolExecutor.kt:1295-1301 ("isEnabled" branch)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Coalesce the evaluateValue result to false when no element matches (or resolve existence first)
- Add a unit test pinning the false-for-missing-selector behaviour for all three is-* commands
- Document the return value of each assertion in its help page

issues.title: highlight/scrollintoview missing-element errors are labeled [TIMEOUT] and dump internal Java signatures

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval highlight "#no-such-element-abc"   (and scrollintoview with the same selector; fails in ~3.8s)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A clear failure that names the user's command and the selector, e.g. 'highlight failed: no element matches "#no-such-element-abc"'.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Prints '[TIMEOUT] browser_evaluate failed: No element matches selector "#no-such-element-abc". help: Evaluate JavaScript in the page, or against the element matched by selector.' followed by the full Java signature of tab.evaluateValue(...) and its argument docs. Exit code is correct (1) and the selector is named, but the code suggests a slow operation rather than a bad selector, the leaked tool name is the internal `browser_evaluate` (not the user's `highlight`), and the signature dump reads like a debug stack.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: highlight/scrollintoview are eval-based shortcuts (commands.rs:2283-2290) whose element wait throws a TimeoutException when the selector never appears; ToolErrorMapper.classify checks exception types before message patterns, so TimeoutException wins over the 'No element matches selector' text (ToolErrorCode.kt:105-111). MCPToolController.buildErrorMessage then appends the static tool spec because the failure passes isUsageError (MCPToolController.kt:1961) — even though its own comment says the spec should be reserved for usage errors.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-agentic/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agentic/tools/ToolErrorCode.kt:105-111; browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/mcp/controller/MCPToolController.kt:1942-1966; cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2283

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Classify 'No element matches selector' as TARGET_UNAVAILABLE/NOT_FOUND with precedence over the timeout type mapping, or convert the never-appeared-selector wait timeout into the no-match error at the source
- Suppress the tool-spec/signature dump on runtime errors (as the code comment already intends)
- Use the user-facing command name (highlight/scrollintoview) instead of the internal tool name in the message

issues.title: pushstate silently fails (exit 0) on a URL the browser refuses, and gives no warning when the pushed URL is not served

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval pushstate "https://example.com/other"  -> prints 'null' + generic hint, exit 0, location.href unchanged. Also: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval pushstate "/b4/definitely-missing-xyz.html" (404 on the server) -> URL printed, exit 0, no warning.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A cross-origin pushState throws SecurityError in the page, so the command should fail with a clear message and non-zero exit; the help should state that only the client-side URL changes (content stays), and ideally an advisory should appear when the pushed path returns 404.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The command printed `null` followed by a generic '💡 Expression returned null. The queried element or property may not exist on this page. Try verifying: eval "document.querySelector(...)"' hint and exited 0, while location.href was provably unchanged. The 404 push reported success with no warning at all.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: pushstate is implemented as browser_evaluate of `() => { history.pushState({}, '', "<url>"); return location.href; }` (commands.rs:2268). The SecurityError aborts before the return, the expression result is null, and the CLI's null-result path treats a null result as a successful call and emits the element/property-oriented hint; it never re-checks location.href.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2263-2270 (pushstate tool_params_fn); CLI null-result hint path in cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Have the CLI verify location.href after the push and fail non-zero with a targeted message when it did not change ('cross-origin URLs cannot be pushed; use goto for navigation')
- Suppress the generic element/property null hint for pushstate, or replace it with pushstate-specific guidance
- State explicitly in the help that the page content does not change and that a pushed URL is never fetched from the server

issues.title: get box output contradicts the documented {x, y, width, height} shape

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval get box "#scroll-target"   and   ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval get box "#scroll-target" --json

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: `--help get` says: 'box — returns the bounding box {x, y, width, height} of the first matching element.' A JSON object with those four numeric keys.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: {"type":"ai.platon.pulsar.common.math.geometric.RectD","description":"RectD(x=24.0, y=2159.0, width=1857.0, height=24.0)"} — a Java toString wrapper. Even --json nests it as an opaque string in output.result, so scripts must string-parse the description. The coordinate space (viewport-relative; y changed 2159→824 when scrollY changed 0→1335) is also undocumented.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The "boundingBox" branch returns the RectD object itself (BrowserTabToolExecutor.kt:2342-2349) and the MCP response serializer renders unsupported types as {type, description} rather than decomposing the fields.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-agentic/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agentic/tools/builtin/BrowserTabToolExecutor.kt:2342-2349; help text in cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs (get command notes)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Return a plain map {x, y, width, height} (numbers) instead of the RectD object, so both text and --json output match the documented contract
- Document that coordinates are viewport-relative in the get help page
- Add a test asserting the JSON shape of `get box`

issues.title: Unknown/typo'd options and extra positionals are silently ignored

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval is visible "#hidden-target" --bogus-xyz  (also --fail-on-false, and an extra positional); ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval check "#check-target" --no-snapshott (typo); ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval open --headlesss <url>

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: An unknown option should be rejected (or at least warned about) naming the offending flag; an extra positional argument should be an error.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: All silently accepted, exit 0. The typo'd --no-snapshot still performed the snapshot (visible in the output), and --headlesss silently fell back to the default display mode. This also masks the absence of a --fail-on-false flag (it looks accepted but does nothing). Contrast: the CLI deliberately rejects stray global flags and a trailing `-s` per the documented session rules, so rejection is not uniformly absent.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Argument parsing for commands with no declared options drops unrecognized --flags and leftover positionals instead of raising 'unknown option'. CommandDef option lists exist (e.g. check declares --no-snapshot) but unknown names are not validated against them.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (command argument parsing / option matching against CommandDef.options)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Reject unknown options with exit 2 and a did-you-mean suggestion (closest option name)
- Reject extra positional arguments with 'unexpected argument' + usage (the wording already exists for stray global flags)
- Warn when a known option is applied to a command that does not use it

issues.title: --help <command> --examples never loads tool-level examples and misdiagnoses it as 'is the backend running?'

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 --help click --examples  and  ./b4w.ps1 --help check --examples  (backend healthy; `status` shows Server health: UP)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Runnable examples, or an accurate reason when none exist.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: 'Examples for browser4-cli click (built into the CLI): …' followed by 'Tool-level examples are unavailable: is the backend running?' — and for check/focus/scrollintoview/highlight/pushstate/is visible/is enabled the entire response is 'No examples available for 'X' — is the backend running?'. Every command help page advertises this route as 'Runnable examples: browser4-cli X --help --examples'. curl http://127.0.0.1:8283/mcp/tools/specs returns 200 with {"tools":[]} on this backend.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: build_tool_examples fetches GET /mcp/tools/specs and maps an empty spec list to 'is the backend running?' (main.rs:21327-21334). That endpoint only lists plugin-declared specs with a non-blank cliName (MCPToolController.kt:640-647), so it is empty on a stock build without plugins — while the backend ships examples for built-in tab tools (TabToolExamples.kt, including isVisible/isChecked/isEnabled). The CLI therefore reports a healthy backend as down.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:21327-21334 (build_tool_examples); browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/mcp/controller/MCPToolController.kt:640-647 (listCliToolSpecs)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Include built-in tool specs (or at least their examples) in /mcp/tools/specs, or expose them via a second endpoint the CLI consults
- Distinguish 'spec list empty' from 'fetch failed' — never claim the backend is down when the HTTP call succeeded
- Add CLI-bundled examples for the core commands (check, uncheck, focus, scrollintoview, highlight, pushstate, is visible/enabled/checked)

Needs investigation: check the backend sessions endpoint used to populate the column and whether the CLI maps sessionId to the active tab URL (per-session page lookup may not be wired for the 'Browser4' connection type).

issues.title: highlight outlines accumulate and cannot be cleared

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval highlight "#click-target" ; ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval highlight "#dblclick-target" ; then eval both elements' style.outline

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Either only one element is highlighted at a time, or there is a documented way to remove the marker (e.g. `unhighlight`).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Both elements now carry 'rgb(255, 87, 34) solid 3px' as an inline style, persisting indefinitely. No unhighlight/clear command exists and the help does not mention that the marker survives (screenshots and visual checks after a highlight will include the orange outline).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The highlight expression sets element.style.outline directly (commands.rs:2287) with no bookkeeping of the previous target and no cleanup path or removal command.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:2283-2290 (highlight expression)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Clear the previous highlight (or all highlights) on each highlight call, or add `unhighlight [selector]` / `--clear`
- Document in the help that the outline is an inline style mutation that persists until removed
- Consider using an overlay element rather than mutating the page's own style

issues.title: --help-json rejects the spaced command name and returns error payloads with exit 0

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 --help-json "is visible"  ->  {"error":"Unknown command: is visible"}, EXIT=0 ; compare ./b4w.ps1 --help "is visible" (works)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Same name forms accepted as text help (the displayed name 'is visible', the internal 'is-visible'), and an error payload should exit non-zero for scripts.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The JSON mode resolves only the internal hyphenated key; the error object is emitted with exit 0, and the JSON payload contains no output/exit-code contract for the command even when it resolves.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: --help-json does not run the classify_help_target resolution that the text --help path uses, and its error branch prints JSON without setting a failing exit status.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (help-json handler; classify_help_target at ~21280)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Route --help-json through the same classify_help_target resolution as --help
- Exit non-zero when the JSON payload is an error object
- Include the command's output contract (prints true/false) and exit codes in the JSON metadata

issues.title: Git Bash: ./b4w.ps1 rejects arguments starting with '/' (e.g. pushstate URLs) due to MSYS path conversion

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 -s state-eval pushstate "/b4/frame-other.html"  (Git Bash on Windows)

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The URL is pushed onto the history stack.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Exit 1 with: "Error: argument 'C:/Program Files/Git/b4/frame-other.html' (probably typed as '/b4/frame-other.html') was rewritten by Git Bash's MSYS path conversion before PowerShell started. ... Run this command via ./b4w.sh instead (it disables the conversion). Or export MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' and re-run". Retrying with MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' succeeded. This affects any slash-leading argument (absolute paths, pushstate URLs) and is the first thing a Git-Bash user hits on this command family.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: MSYS2 converts slash-leading arguments into Windows paths before pwsh sees them; b4w.ps1 detects the rewrite and refuses (the safe behavior) but the required b4w.sh / MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL workaround is documented only in CLAUDE.md and the error text, not in the CLI's own help for bash users.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: b4w.ps1 (wrapper guard); b4w.sh (bash wrapper)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Mention the b4w.sh / MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL workaround in the CLI help (or a shell-quoting reference section) for bash users on Windows
- Consider having b4w.ps1 auto-retry by delegating to b4w.sh when it detects the rewrite
- Keep the current fail-loudly diagnostic — it is clear and actionable
